query: For titanium alloys used as structural materials, formulate one hypothesis for an intervention that could increase surface hardness and wear resistance. Specify the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected improvement relative to the untreated alloy, the service or test conditions under which the effect should hold, prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and a controlled experiment with clear results that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Reactive electrospark deposition (RESD) using low-melting Al-Si alloys as electrodes can increase the surface hardness and wear resistance of titanium alloys used as structural materials.
generation.material_initial_state: Titanium alloy (Ti6Al4V or Ti-GR5) or commercially pure titanium (Ti-GR2) with surface roughness Ra = 10-15 μm or Ra = 8-12 μm.
generation.intervention: Reactive electrospark deposition (RESD) using low-melting Al-Si alloys as electrodes.
generation.conditions: Equipment with low-pulse energy (E = 0.01-0.07 J), semi-automatic non-contact local electrospark deposition (LESD) or manual ESD via reciprocating movement of the electrode.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a local liquid reaction phase on the surface of the substrate, resulting in the synthesis of new phases and the formation of ultra-dispersed, amorphous, and nanoscale structures.
generation.mechanism: The extremely high cooling rate of the reactive melt (10^5-10^6 °C/s) allows the formation of new structures with improved wear resistance.
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased surface hardness and wear resistance of the titanium alloy.
generation.baseline: Untreated titanium alloy with surface roughness Ra = 10-15 μm or Ra = 8-12 μm.
generation.boundary: The effect should hold under normal atmospheric conditions, without heating, thermal impact, and deformation of the layered product.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal parameters for the RESD process, such as the pulse energy, electrode material, and deposition speed, are not fully understood and require further study.

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled experiment comparing the surface hardness and wear resistance of titanium alloys treated with RESD using low-melting Al-Si alloys as electrodes versus untreated titanium alloys.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the surface hardness and wear resistance of the treated titanium alloys are not significantly higher than those of the untreated alloys, the hypothesis is falsified.

However, two main reasons prevent the wider application of AM–PBF-LB/M for the production of titanium products.
The first reason is the low hardness and low tribological characteristics of titanium alloys, which limit the scope of their application. Attempts of researchers to avoid them by creating new alloys or appropriate heat treatment have not yet led to satisfactory results [,,]. Currently, issues of surface quality control of SLM and DMLS products, as well as improving the surface characteristics of titanium and its alloys, are becoming increasingly relevant.
Electrospark deposition (ESD) is a suitable and ecological method for improving the surface quality and surface characteristics of titanium SLM and DMLS products. Along with a possibility of controlled production of coatings with a wide range of compositions, structures, and parameters, compared to existing methods for applying wear-resistant coatings, the main advantages of ESD [,] are the high adhesion of coatings to the titanium substrate, the possibility of local surface treatment to apply the coatings on external surfaces of any shape and size in strictly defined locations without the need for means and measures to protect the rest of the surface of the product, the ease of deposition under normal atmospheric conditions, the lack of heating, the thermal impact and deformation of the layered product and its high environmental resistance, the uni

ing transfer is in mixed vapour, liquid and solid (from brittle breakage of the electrode) states. At the hard alloy electrodes, the presence of the transferred solid phase is relatively high and at such a rate of mass transfer, the formed coatings usually have increased roughness compared to that of the substrate. To reduce the roughness, in this work, reactive electrospark deposition (RESD) [,,] was carried out. The purpose of RESD is to form a local liquid reaction phase on the surface of the substrate, in which the components of the electrode and the substrate actively mix, fill the voids and pores and distribute evenly on the layered surface, reacting with each other to form new phases.
Signs of active interaction of the electrode and substrate material under conditions of local melting in the ESD process, in which the properties of the substrate are improved as a result of the synthesis of new phases, have been noted in many works [,,,,]. In addition, the extremely high cooling rate of the reactive melt (105–106 °C/s) [,,] allows the formation of new ultra-dispersed, amorphous and nanoscale structures with improved wear resistance. ## 2.2. Equipment and Conditions of ESD
It is widely known [,,,] that the characteristics and properties of electrospark coatings depend mainly on the material of the electrode and the electrical parameters of the deposition mode (current, voltage, capacity, duration and frequency of the pulses, which are most often expressed by the energy of the unit impulse, or impulse energy, E). The increase in the values of the electrical parameters of the mode, respective to the pulse energy, causes an increase in the thickness and roughness of the coatings. To obtain smoother surfaces in the present research, equipment with low-pulse energy was used, i.e., E = 0.01–0.07 J. Two ESD schemes were used.
